answer:
The NeuroArm is an MRI‑compatible robotic platform that includes a controller, a robot with two 7‑degree‑of‑freedom arms (each equipped with a 1‑DOF piezoelectric‑motor tool), and a workstation for surgeon operation. It uses a master‑slave configuration in which the surgeon’s hand‑held stylus movements are replicated by the tool tip, provides audio, visual and tactile (haptic) feedback via a multiaxis force‑sensing system, and incorporates an attached microscope for detailed viewing [Source: Document [1] | Source: Evolution-of-Robotics-in-Medical-Surgeries-and-Health-Care-Systems-A-Review.pdf, Page 4].

The system is capable of performing microsurgery and image‑guided biopsy, as well as fine suturing, thermocoagulation, and other operations such as stereotactic procedures [Source: Document [1] | Source: Evolution-of-Robotics-in-Medical-Surgeries-and-Health-Care-Systems-A-Review.pdf, Page 4].
ground_truth: NeuroArm is an MRI-compatible surgical system with two 7-DOF arms and haptic feedback, capable of microsurgery, image-guided biopsy, fine suturing, and thermocoagulation.

radiation in large amounts and concentrating them on the 
tumor infested areas. When the beams are used to treat tumors 
in the brain and spine it is called Stereotactic radiosurgery 
(SRS) and when used to treat tumors on other parts of the 
body outside the brain and spine area, it is called Stereotactic 
body radiation therapy (SBRT) [60, 61]. Radiosurgery is also 
known as CyberKnife or Gamma Knife which is named after 
the machines being used. CT scans and MRI give the precise 
location of a tumor which is in relation to skeletal landmarks 
or fiducial markers that are implanted [62]. Establishing the 
exact location of the landmarks is crucial and challenging.A

is used for identifying the landmarks. It is locked in position 
with respect to the treatment device [62]. This method 
enables the tumor to be centered inside a sphere of multiple', 'The Gamma Knife is a minimally invasive SRS device that 
focuses on the treatment of cancerous and non-cancerous 
tumors which was developed in 1969 by Elekta AB. It 
provides a painless alternative to the conventional surgery. It 
consists of a lightweight stereotactic head frame which has a 
3-D coordinate system and is fixed onto the patients head. A 
collimator helmet consisting of 201 holes is fitted onto the 
head frame. The treatment begins with the patient undergoing 
a CT, MRI or angiography scan in order to locate the lesions. 
Locating the tumors is a crucial step [63]. The results are sent 
over to the planning computer system which give the 3-D 
coordinates of the tumor. The identified location is then 
exposed to 201 individual gamma beams of cobalt-60 [63, 65, 
66]. These beams are focused onto the centre of a collimator 
helmet to deliver a high concentration of radiation with low 
irradiation of proximal structures. The beam is selected based 
on the shape of the tumor and its intensity is chosen on the 
duration of exposure. Treatment is performed in a single 
session which can extend from 20 minutes up to 2 hours [67]. 
Its accuracy is up to 0.3 mm [68]. Upon completion of the 
treatment, the head frame gets removed and the patient is 
moved out of the machine automatically. The whole 
procedure is painless. The main limitation of this device is

answer:
The CyberKnife is a frameless stereotactic radiosurgery system developed by Accuray that delivers radiation beams with sub‑millimetre accuracy to both cancerous and non‑cancerous tumors throughout the body (brain, spine, kidney, pancreas, prostate, liver, etc.) using a robotic arm and a soft‑mesh mask for patient setup【Source: Document [3], Page 12】.  

Its primary advantage over the Gamma Knife is that it does not require a rigid stereotactic head frame and is not limited to intracranial lesions; it can treat tumors in any part of the body, providing a non‑invasive, painless option with flexible beam delivery【Source: Document [3], Page 12】【Source: Document [2], Page 11】.
ground_truth: CyberKnife is a frameless stereotactic radiosurgery alternative to Gamma Knife that uses a robotic arm with a linear accelerator and motion tracking to treat tumors non-invasively anywhere in the body.
